concerns.note: Observation: in consecutive frames1630–1659 and every-third-frame1660–1705, especially native1650,1665,1680, the chapel and candle image split together into thin, straight-edged, rotating planes. Impact: the passage clearly ruptures and exposes the violent world, but its physical reading is closer to a shattered picture than falling architectural masonry; this is the strongest visual counterargument to the requested church collapse. It remains an expressive concern, because falling fragments, exposure of the lava route, and transition into the new world are visibly present. Minimum remedy if physical masonry becomes essential in a later authorized request: keep the candle coherent while restricting fractures to architecture and giving the nearest fragments modest thickness/back-face shading; this would require renderer work, not a metadata edit. Confirmation: review consecutive encoded frames around1637–1705 at native resolution and phone size, showing recognizable architectural fragments dropping away without obscuring the lava route. The editor may accept the current stylized rupture on the observed evidence; no new repair is assumed here.
